title.narrative: ACCH - CREALA: Climate resilience and advocacy in Latin America

description.narrative: CREALA is an initiative that will be developed in Honduras and Guatemala in the Central American isthmus of Latin America. It develops two of the priority objectives for Latin America: resilience and climate impact, from a local to a global approach.CREALA is implemented by two partners, ACCH and CASM. It incorporates direct actions with 200 small families of basic grains and coffee producers, influencing their livelihoods with the incorporation of good adaptation practices for climate monitoring and community organisation. At the same time, advocacy processes on the climate agenda with a reach of some 20,000 people addressed in local and regional platforms such as the Vulnerable Central America Forum, FOSPA, CANLA and others. These platforms will become social channels for consultation, awareness raising, exchange, cohesion and action on the climate agenda in the region. In terms of advocacy and lobbying, the project will contribute to improving the visibility of the demands and perspectives of vulnerable population segments in the face of climate change in national, regional and international decision-making spaces. To this end, it will increase the participation and improve the capacity of civil society organisations in the region (Latin America and the Caribbean) to participate in national consultation processes and in institutionalised regional and international spaces in which the governments of countries in the region debate and adopt decisions that to a large extent determine the sustainability, destruction or improvement of the livelihoods of communities. The project identifies the nexus between gender equality, social inclusion and climate justice. It includes greater participation of women and youth in these networks, as well as contributing to strengthening women's leadership in advocacy spaces. Women will be made visible in the front line for the defence of territories, their contribution to the care of society and ecosystems, ecofeminism, criminalisation of women human rights defenders and the rights of indigenous peoples (the project will work with indigenous Chortis women in Honduras).
